fed_news.headline: Fed's Musalem says he won't prejudge September rate call
fed_news.summary: St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said he would keep an open mind on the September 15-16 decision, while describing policy as accommodative and saying underlying inflation remained between 2.5% and 3%, above the Fed's 2% target.

fed_news.headline: Fed minutes show many officials saw a hike as necessary if inflation failed to cool
fed_news.summary: The Federal Reserve released minutes from the July 28-29 FOMC meeting. The minutes said several policymakers were ready to raise rates and many believed a hike would be needed if inflation did not decline, after the committee voted 9-3 to hold at 3.50%-3.75%.

fed_news.headline: Global brokerages diverge on the Fed policy path
fed_news.summary: Reuters reported that more research firms were forecasting at least one Fed hike this year, while futures were pricing nearly a 35% chance of a 25bp September hike, down from 48.4% a week earlier; Wells Fargo Investment Institute became the latest firm to forecast a hike.

fed_news.headline: Fed expected to leave rates unchanged next month after soft inflation data
fed_news.summary: Reuters reported that July CPI rose 3.4% year over year and core CPI slowed to 2.5%, leading traders to add to bets for no change at the September 15-16 FOMC meeting; futures still priced a 38% chance of a hike at that point.

fed_news.headline: Fading Fed hike bets after weak July jobs data put September decision back in play
fed_news.summary: Reuters reported that fed funds futures implied a 44% probability of a September 15-16 rate hike, down from 55% before the weak July employment report; investors are awaiting the July CPI release.

fed_news.headline: US rate futures cut chances of September Fed hike after weak jobs data
fed_news.summary: Reuters reported that rate futures reduced the probability of a September Fed tightening to 43.9% from 57% before the July jobs report, while the reported hold probability rose to 60.4% from 43.2%.

fed_news.headline: Soft July jobs report fuels skepticism over possible Fed rate hike
fed_news.summary: Reuters said the U.S. unexpectedly shed jobs in July and prior payrolls were revised sharply lower, with futures pricing roughly 40% odds of a September hike versus 55% before the report.

fed_news.headline: Fed's Cook ready to raise rates if inflation doesn't start easing
fed_news.summary: Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook said she was prepared to raise the policy rate if inflation does not start cooling, while noting that holding rates unchanged at the July meeting was appropriate while officials assess incoming data.

fed_news.headline: Fed officials send mixed signals ahead of the September meeting
fed_news.summary: Reuters reported that Governor Lisa Cook was open to raising rates if inflation stays too high, while San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly was comfortable with the July hold as the Fed waits for more data.

fed_news.headline: Fed's Schmid says tighter policy needed to bring inflation back to 2%
fed_news.summary: Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid said tighter monetary policy is needed to bring inflation back to the Fed's 2% target. Schmid does not currently vote on the FOMC; his remarks followed last week's 9-3 hold.

fed_news.headline: Kashkari says the Fed should start moving rates up gradually
fed_news.summary: Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari said higher rates are needed now and that a gradual move could begin in September. Kashkari was one of the three dissenters who favored a 25bp hike at the July FOMC meeting.

fed_news.headline: Fed rate hike odds rise to 65% for September meeting, Reuters reports
fed_news.summary: Reuters reported that Fed funds futures implied a 65% probability of a 25bp hike at the September 15-16 FOMC meeting. No new FOMC decision or statement was issued since the July 29 hold.

fed_news.headline: Fed's Williams expects inflation to ease, says Fed will act if it doesn't
fed_news.summary: New York Fed President John Williams said inflation should ease gradually toward the Fed's 2% goal, but the central bank would not hesitate to raise rates if inflation fails to cool. He strongly supported the July hold and said policy is well positioned.

fed_news.headline: Treasury selloff signals need to bolster Fed's inflation credibility, Musalem tells Reuters
fed_news.summary: St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said the Treasury selloff underscored the need to reinforce the Fed's inflation credibility. Reuters reported that CME FedWatch implied a 67% chance of a 25bp hike at the September meeting.

fed_news.headline: Fed dissenters sketch the case for a rate hike
fed_news.summary: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said she dissented in favor of a 25bp hike because inflation remained too high and was unlikely to return to target without tighter policy. She was one of three officials who dissented at the July meeting.

fed_news.headline: J.P.Morgan brings forward Fed rate hike call to December after July hold
fed_news.summary: J.P. Morgan now expects a quarter-point hike in December 2026 rather than in the second half of 2027, while flagging September hike risk remains live if inflation continues to run hot. Markets priced a 65.2% chance of a September hike, down from 81% before the July statement.

fed_news.headline: Dollar recovers as Fed holds rates, US strikes Iran
fed_news.summary: The dollar steadied after the Fed's hold decision and a US strike on Iran-linked targets added to geopolitical risk premium in markets. Fed funds futures imply a 42.6% probability of a hold at the September meeting, compared with 24% before the July decision.

fed_news.headline: The most hawkish split in a decade: the Fed holds steady with three dissents
fed_news.summary: The FOMC held the target range at 3.50%-3.75% on a 9-3 vote, the most divided vote in over a decade, with three regional presidents dissenting in favor of an immediate 25bp hike. Odds of a September hike stood near 70% pre-decision on CME FedWatch.

fed_news.headline: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady at July FOMC meeting
fed_news.summary: The Fed held its target range at 3.50%-3.75% for a fifth consecutive meeting, in a 9-3 vote with three dissents favoring a hike. Chair Kevin Warsh held a press conference at 2:30pm ET. No meeting is scheduled in August; the next meeting is September 15-16, 2026.

fed_news.headline: What a divided Fed means for investors
fed_news.summary: Following the hawkish hold, Fed funds futures suggested a more than 57% likelihood of a quarter-point hike at the September meeting, per CME's FedWatch tool. About 53% of Kalshi traders predicted a hike versus 43% for another hold.

fed_news.headline: Fed's hawkish hold and global market reactions
fed_news.summary: Treasury yields jumped after the decision, with the 30-year approaching its highest level since 2007 near 5.10%, and futures pricing roughly a 76% chance of a September rate increase.
